extracted.intended_audience: school and college administrators, Title IX coordinators, decision-makers, and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance describing standards, procedures, and required content for recipients' Title IX sexual harassment grievance processes, including evidentiary standards and required written determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible standards of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may choose either the preponderance of the evidence standard or the clear and convincing evidence standard (but not a standard lower than preponderance or higher than clear and convincing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both standards are "standards common to civil proceedings" and differ only in degree of confidence required. The Department determined that either can produce accurate determinations when applied within a fair grievance process. The Department declines to define these standards in the regulations, intending their traditional civil-context meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice of chosen evidentiary standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must notify its students and employees in advance of the standard of evidence the recipient will apply in sexual harassment grievance processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice fosters a fair, reliable outcome and legitimacy. The Department expects recipients to select a standard based on what best serves their educational community, applicable State law, or collective bargaining agreements; the Department does not require recipients to explain their rationale publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same evidentiary standard for student and employee cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must use the same standard of evidence to reach determinations regarding responsibility in Title IX proceedings against students as they do for Title IX proceedings against employees, including all staff and faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same standard must apply to each formal complaint alleging sexual harassment responded to by a particular recipient, whether the respondent is a student or an employee. This provision was retained even though the Department removed a prior NPRM limitation tying use of preponderance to non-Title IX matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on extremes in evidentiary standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations prohibit recipients from adopting an evidentiary standard lower than preponderance of the evidence or higher than clear and convincing evidence for Title IX formal complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department concluded that standards lower than preponderance or higher than clear and convincing would not appropriately balance the needs for reliability and fairness in Title IX processes given the stakes for both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determination regarding responsibility required
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers are required to provide a written determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring a written determination prevents confusion, provides a record for appeals and review, protects due process, reduces bias, and promotes thoroughness and independent decision-making. The Department declined requests to exempt smaller institutions or elementary/secondary schools from this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous delivery of written determination to parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination regarding responsibility must be provided to the parties simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simultaneous provision promotes transparency and equal treatment of the parties and gives both parties the same information for appeals or further proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of the written determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must include: identification of allegations potentially constituting sexual harassment as defined in §106.30; the procedural steps taken from receipt of the formal complaint through the determination regarding responsibility; findings of fact supporting the determination; conclusions regarding application of the recipient's code of conduct to the facts of conduct alleged to constitute Title IX sexual harassment; a determination regarding responsibility for each allegation and the decision-maker's rationale for the result; any disciplinary sanctions the recipient imposes on the respondent and whether the recipient will provide remedies to the complainant; and information regarding the appeals process and the recipient's procedures and permissible bases for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements promote transparency and understanding of how allegations were resolved and are intended to be adequate for appeals or judicial review. The Department revised prior proposed language to reference allegations as defined in §106.30 rather than sections of the recipient's code of conduct to avoid confusion about scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural steps must be described in the written determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must describe the procedural steps of the investigation (e.g., notifications to parties, interviews of parties and witnesses, site visits, methods used to gather evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although commenters noted this has no direct analogue in criminal/civil procedure, the Department requires these procedural details in the written determination so both parties understand how the investigative process led to the decision and can raise procedural irregularities on appeal. The investigative report itself is required to fairly summarize relevant evidence but is not required to include the investigator's timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of relevant evidence and avoidance of status-based credibility inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers and investigators are obligated to objectively evaluate all relevant evidence, including inculpatory and exculpatory evidence, and to avoid credibility inferences based on a person's status as a complainant, respondent, or witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to require the written determination to recite contradictory facts, exculpatory evidence, or all evidence presented; instead objective evaluation under §106.45(b)(1)(ii) provides the basis for the decision-maker's rationale described in the written determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of sanctions and remedies in written determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must identify any disciplinary sanctions the recipient imposes on the respondent and whether the recipient will provide remedies to the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters raised FERPA and safety/privacy concerns about disclosing remedies; the Department nevertheless requires inclusion of sanctions and whether remedies will be provided, and notes recipients retain discretion in how they describe application of their own code of conduct to the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency for appeals and judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must be adequate to allow the parties and any appellate reviewer to understand the basis for the determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department believes §106.45(b)(7) as revised provides sufficient description of rationale and findings for appeal or judicial review without prescribing overly prescriptive findings-of-fact language; the decision-maker's rationale for 'the result' must be described.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to define evidentiary standards in regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to provide formal regulatory definitions of 'preponderance of the evidence' and 'clear and convincing evidence' and intends each standard to have its traditional civil/administrative meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters who sought explicit regulatory definitions were declined because the Department considers the terms to have commonly understood meanings in other legal contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' discretion in selecting the evidentiary standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may select their evidentiary standard based on what best serves their educational community, applicable State law, or bargained-for standards with unionized employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will not require recipients to explain publicly why they selected a particular standard, though recipients are not precluded from communicating their rationale to their community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department will not impose discovery-like processes or subpoena powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not impose court-like discovery rules or create subpoena powers to compel parties or witnesses to be interviewed or testify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid making educational institutions mimic courts, the Department refrains from imposing discovery rules; instead, the written determination and investigative report serve to ensure parties understand the evidence and procedural steps used to reach the decision.
